standard_prerequisites.name: Linearised operator symbol
standard_prerequisites.statement: The symbol of the linearised operator is given by an integral over the positive half-line of an exponential factor, a sine factor and the Fourier transform of the background.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the quantity whose decay and boundedness are asserted.

standard_prerequisites.name: Sobolev norms with a weight
standard_prerequisites.statement: The norms appearing in the statement carry a derivative count, an extra positive power of one half and a logarithmic weight controlled by a parameter delta zero.
standard_prerequisites.use: They are the norms that bound the symbol in the three parts of the statement.

standard_prerequisites.name: Directional integral estimate
standard_prerequisites.statement: The directional integrals of derivatives of the background obey a bound by the weighted Sobolev norm, uniformly in the direction.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the estimate invoked in the first part of the proof.

core_obligations: Observe first that the symbol vanishes at zero frequency, so that only non-zero frequencies have to be treated (source line 1108).

For the first two parts, bound the symbol by the absolute value of the Fourier transform of the background times a directional integral of the background, absorbing the sine factor by its argument, and then apply the directional integral estimate (source lines 1109-1115).
Read the decay in the large parameter from the Riemann-Lebesgue property of the Fourier transform of a function in the first Lebesgue space (source line 1115).

For the third part, integrate the integral representation by parts in the radial variable, no boundary term surviving, and bound the two resulting terms by the sharper weighted norm (source lines 1117-1129).
Note that the classical limit satisfies the same bounds with identical estimates (source line 1130).

proof_roadmap.step: Bound by the directional integral estimate and read off decay and uniform boundedness.
Integrate by parts for the sharper bound, then extend to the classical limit.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's labelled lemma at source lines 1092-1106, which has three parts: uniform decay of the linearised operator symbol in the large parameter, a uniform bound in the weighted Sobolev norm of the background, and a sharper bound with an extra factor of the parameter over the modulus of the spectral variable once the background lies in one more weighted space. The proof (source lines 1107-1131) first removes the zero frequency, then absorbs the sine factor by its argument to reduce the first two parts to a directional integral estimate, and finally integrates the integral representation of the symbol by parts in the radial variable, where it has to be checked that no boundary term survives and that the two resulting terms are controlled by the sharper norm. The statement records none of these reductions.
